_README: Organisations worth finding ONE person at, to ask how they got into
offshore rotational work. This is not a target list for applications -
ask_around.py asks a question and never asks for a job.
NO NAMES IN THIS FILE, DELIBERATELY. Writing 'ask Dave the ops manager'
would be me inventing a person, and a letter to an invented person is
worse than no letter. ask_around.py finds a real named individual with a
published address on the organisation's own site, MX-checks it, and
writes to nobody at all if it cannot find one.
'why' is the line that goes into the letter after 'I am writing to you
because...'. It has to be TRUE of that organisation and checkable by the
person reading it - they will know instantly if it is filler, and filler
is what makes a letter look sent rather than written.
Three kinds of organisation are here, for three different answers:
SKILLS BODIES AND TRAINING - their actual job is getting people in,
and they know which routes are funded, which is Harry's live problem.
ROV AND SUBSEA CONTRACTORS - closest to what he already does at
Sonardyne, and the likeliest honest route offshore for him.
OPERATORS - who decide what a contractor's crew must hold, so they
know what the real minimum is rather than what an advert asks for.
SONARDYNE IS DELIBERATELY NOT ON THIS LIST. It was, for a moment: he works
there and the people there know the kit. But a cold email to your current
employer asking how to get out of the workshop and offshore is a message
that can reach a line manager, and the downside is not a wasted approach -
it is the job he already has. That conversation is worth having, in person,
when he chooses. ask_around.py also refuses his employer in code, so adding
it back to this file is not enough to send one.

organisations.why: OPITO sets the BOSIET and MIST standards themselves, so you will know better than anyone whether there is a sensible order to do them in for someone not yet offshore
you work across the whole North Sea industry rather than one operator, so you see where people actually come in from
you train the people going offshore for the first time, so you meet more first-timers than anyone
you both train people and crew jobs, which is an unusual view of how someone gets their first rotation
you see people coming into offshore work from other industries and from the forces
ROV work is the closest thing offshore to what I already do onshore at Sonardyne, and I would like to know whether that reads as relevant experience or not
your ROV crews use the kind of acoustic positioning kit I build and fault-find, and I want to know whether that counts for anything on the way in
your survey and ROV crews are the nearest offshore equivalent of the workshop side I already know
you rent and support subsea instrumentation offshore, which is the trade I already have onshore
you crew a lot of offshore technician work in the North Sea and I want to understand what the real minimum is to be considered
you supply offshore maintenance crews across the North Sea, so you will know what an electrical technician actually needs to hold before anyone will take him
you crew offshore maintenance across the North Sea and will know whether an onshore electrical background is a way in or a dead end
as the operator you decide what a contractor's crew must hold, so you know the real minimum rather than what an advert asks for
you operate North Sea platforms directly, so you see what the crews coming aboard actually have behind them
you run North Sea assets with a small team, so you will have a clear view of what a technician needs before he is any use offshore
you operate in the North Sea and take on technicians through contractors, so you see who makes it and who does not
